notes: Three tabs now: AI Analyzer, AI Photo, Guide. The Side View tab is gone — its side-view tip (phone square to the lane, 10–15 ft away, full body in frame) lives in the AI Analyzer.
When an analysis finishes, AI Photo and Guide get a red “New” badge, and the AI Analyzer shows “Analysis done — see your AI Photo report and your new fix in Guide.” Opening a tab clears its badge.
Guide now shows “Your latest fix” from the run you just finished, at the top.

AI Photo is connected to the AI Analyzer: it shows your latest run (reps, top fixes, best/worst frames), and every photo gets pointing markers — green checks where form looks good, a red mark where to work — plus “What looks good” and “Work on” lists in plain words. If a joint is out of frame, it says which one instead of guessing.

Your form vs Pro form — watch the run: a 2D animated demo on a runway in AI Photo. Your character runs with your measured angles, the pro runs with ideal angles, and the callout shows your actual top fix. 2D drawing from measured angles — not real 3D, not your real video. Play / Pause / Replay included.

Knowledge base grown from 26 to 40 entries: finish & lean, sprint hurdles, 400m hurdles, 4×100m, 4×400m, pole vault basics, safe jump landings, shot put glide + rotation, hammer basics, javelin approach, 800m, 1500m / mile, 5000m.

Rep check merged into AI Analyzer: the separate block is gone. One “What to check” pick (Block start, Side-angle sprint, A-skip, Arm action, Sprint form) sets both the live coaching and the rep check. One camera, one Start / Stop flow, one score + one fix.

Live skeleton on the camera: a flat 2D drawing sits on top of the preview while you record — problem joint in red, good joints in green. Still in your results on best + worst frames too. Never fake 3D.

Recording, plainly named: the button says “Start recording”, the status says “Recording…”, and 1 finger starts recording + analyzing while 2 fingers stop it. Buttons do exactly what the hand signs do.
Voice says “Recording has started” and “Recording has ended” when recording starts and stops — with the hand signs or the buttons — even when voice coaching is off.
Upload a clip lives inside the AI Analyzer now (one option, same analysis), plus slow review and switch camera in the same controls.
One AI Analyzer screen: the old Analyze tab and the two-camera tab are gone — live coaching, two cameras, photo check, and your results all live here now. Nothing was removed.
Hands-free gestures: look at the camera and hold up 1 finger to start coaching, 2 fingers to stop. Hold about 1 second. Buttons always work too.

Deep check after every workout: after you stop, the app re-reads the full clip and gives a per-rep breakdown, best + worst frames, and measurements it can actually support — estimates are labeled, and it never invents a speed or a distance.
Videos to watch: after the deep check, 1–2 videos matched to your top fix, from the videos already in the app.
Skeleton drawings in your results: a flat 2D drawing from the camera (never fake 3D) on the best and worst frames, with the joint to fix in red. Tap a red joint to see its fix.
Simpler words everywhere: buttons say what they do, errors say what happened and what to tap next.

AI Analyzer tab: live on-device coaching — watches you through the camera (one or both angles), names the activity, gives one fix at a time with cue + drill, rep counting, voice coaching, and a session summary. Embedded track-and-field + workouts knowledge, no API key, never guesses unseen body parts.
Dual-Angle two-camera analysis: connect an iPad as a second camera with a 6-character code, synced recording + auto-stop + synced replay + combined verdict (two 2D views, never fake 3D).
Photo access asks once: Camera / Photo Library preference is remembered, the picker only opens on your tap, and a cancelled pick shows a retry line instead of re-prompting.
Update system: visible version, What's New panel, Check for updates, and an update banner that fires only on real version bumps.
Private rebuild: no-voice on-screen coaching, smooth UI, two-photo GOOD/FIX analyzer, side-view mode, cue memory, partial-body coaching, fix videos.
